text: The Patriots head to Buffalo on Sunday with a depleted secondary and defensive line, having ruled out cornerback Christian Gonzalez and defensive tackle Christian Barmore due to shoulder injuries, prompting Mike Reiss to examine how New England will manage without two key defensive pieces against Josh Allen and the Bills—though the team did elevate safety Mike Brown and cornerback Kindle Vildor from the practice squad to bolster the roster. On offense, there are questions swirling around receiver Romeo Doubs, whom the Patriots signed to a four-year deal back in March, as he continues searching for consistency in the offense through the team's 1-2 start, while quarterback Drake Maye insisted Wednesday that his right shoulder is fine and that his early struggles stem from poor decision-making rather than any physical limitations. The Patriots will have seven questionable players making the trip to Buffalo, and offensive lineman Matt Pryor is joining the offense as the team looks to turn things around in what should be a turnover-conscious matchup against an Allen-led Bills squad that can bounce back from sloppy performances with particular speed and efficiency.
